turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_shg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format) and `shg` (the
    largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, in pm/V).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the LARGEST SHG
tensor component |d_ij| (pm/V), then select the 5 best candidates from the
pool.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I selected candidates by matching them to the strongest noncentrosymmetric chalcogenide/pnictide structure types in the training data, with heavy-anion substitution (Te > Se > S) used as an additional boost signal.

Top structure-motif matches:
- **c073**: Cd/In/T/As telluride analogue of high-training ZnIn3AsSe4 (55.7 pm/V), with Te expected to increase the response.
- **c090**: K14Ta2As8 is essentially the Ta analogue of K14Nb2As8 (68.8 pm/V in training).
- **c030**: Cd4Si4P8 is isostructural with high-training Zn4Si4P8 / Zn4Sn4P8 phosphides.
- **c082**: Al4Hg2Se8 matches the acentric M4Hg2Se8 family; Ga4Hg2Se8 has 72.7 pm/V in training.
- **c056**: In2Ag2Ge2Se8 belongs to the high-response In2Ag2Sn2Se8 / In2Cu2Ge2Se8 selenide family.

Final: c073, c090, c030, c082, c056
